title: A Handful of Coins
statement: A purse contains plenty of coins of three kinds: coins worth $1$ unit, coins worth $3$ units and coins worth $5$ units. Kai takes exactly three coins from the purse, and any of the three coins may be of the same kind. How many different total values can Kai's three coins have?
hints: Find the smallest and the largest total. Can every whole number between them occur?
Use parity. Three odd values always add up to an odd number, so only odd totals from $3$ to $15$ are possible. Check that each of these can actually be made. For example, $9 = 1 + 3 + 5$.
solution:
Each coin is odd, so the total of three coins is odd. It lies between $1+1+1=3$ and $5+5+5=15$. Every odd value in this range occurs:
$$3=1+1+1,\quad 5=1+1+3,\quad 7=1+1+5,\quad 9=1+3+5,\quad 11=1+5+5,\quad 13=3+5+5,\quad 15=5+5+5.$$
So Kai's three coins can have $7$ different total values.
